evals.name: cold-launch-diagnosis
evals.prompt: the app takes forever to open now — like 3 to 4 seconds of blank screen before home paints anything. i'm on the veteran dev scenario with ~5k words saved. it was fine back when i only had a couple hundred. can you work out what's actually causing it and what we'd do about it?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that identifies the AsyncStorage-persisted query cache (JSON.parse + reviveDates over the whole cache at cold launch) as the prime suspect, distinguishes it from unrelated launch costs, proposes shouldDehydrateQuery filtering and/or a narrower persisted set, notes the buster bump if the cache shape changes, and is honest about what was and wasn't measured.
assertions: Identifies the AsyncStorage-persisted query cache (JSON.parse + reviveDates over the whole cache) as the primary cold-launch cost
Cites src/query/queryClient.ts and/or src/query/reviveDates.ts by path
Notes there is no shouldDehydrateQuery filter, so the ENTIRE query cache is written to and read from disk
Proposes persisting less (shouldDehydrateQuery) or moving word data off the JSON/AsyncStorage path
Flags that the buster must be bumped if the persisted cache shape changes incompatibly
Separates measured claims from unmeasured suspicions instead of asserting invented millisecond figures
Warns against the dev-scenario cache multiplier (userState/plan in query keys) inflating cold-launch measurements

evals.name: preemptive-mutation-review
evals.prompt: i'm about to add a useBulkArchiveCards mutation to query/hooks.ts that archives a bunch of selected words at once. before i write it — is the invalidation pattern we use on all the other card mutations going to bite us at 5k words? what should the new one do instead?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize the existing deckCards/words/dueCards invalidation triple as costly at scale, recommend setQueriesData patching for the word-shaped queries since a bulk archive knows exactly which card ids changed, correctly keep dueCards as an invalidate because of its server-side ordering/limit/fill semantics, and use setQueriesData (plural) rather than setQueryData given the userState/activeLang/uid key variants.
assertions: Identifies the existing deckCards/words/dueCards invalidation triple and says plainly that it is costly at 5k words
Explains the cost concretely (full-library paged refetches, multiple serial round trips per write)
Recommends patching the word-shaped queries via setQueriesData instead of invalidating them
Uses setQueriesData (plural) rather than setQueryData, citing the userState/activeLang/uid key variants
Keeps dueCards as an invalidate and explains why (server-side ordering, limit, and fill semantics cannot be recomputed client-side)
Provides a concrete useBulkArchiveCards implementation as code
States the correctness risk or blast radius of the proposed change

evals.name: word-list-audit
evals.prompt: audit the word list screen's data path please. scrolling feels sluggish once you're a few hundred rows in, and there's a visible pause after you archive a word before the row updates. want to know what's worth fixing and in what order.
evals.expected_output: Should separate the two symptoms (scroll vs. post-archive pause) rather than conflating them, trace the archive pause to useSetCardSuspended's invalidation fan-out triggering full-library refetches, note FlatList is already virtualized so scroll cost is likely fetch/derive/row-render rather than list size, and produce a ranked fix list with risk noted.
assertions: Treats the two symptoms (scroll sluggishness vs. post-archive pause) as separate problems with separate causes
Traces the post-archive pause to useSetCardSuspended invalidating words/deckCards/dueCards and the refetch that follows
Notes WordListScreen already uses FlatList, so raw row count is not itself the scroll cause
Examines row-level re-render cost (memoization, keyExtractor, getItemLayout) or the absence of useQuery select narrowing
Delivers an explicitly ranked fix order rather than an unordered list of ideas
States risk or blast radius for at least one proposed fix
Distinguishes what it measured from what it inferred from reading code
